compound.name: baicalein
compound.one_liner: Aglycone of baicalin; studied in people as an isolated compound (phase I tablets).

compound.absorption_bioavailability: In a phase I study of single ascending doses, baicalein reached peak plasma levels in 0.75-3.5 h and was converted to baicalin; about 27 % was eliminated unchanged in faeces and urinary excretion was under 1 % [34].

evidence.claim: Single ascending doses of isolated baicalein were tolerated by healthy volunteers.
evidence.test_article_detail: baicalein chewable tablets, phase I randomised double-blind
evidence.outcome_summary: Eleven mild treatment-related adverse events, none serious (72 enrolled).
evidence.note: A tolerability/PK study, not an efficacy trial.

processing_stability.note: Formed from baicalin by gut-bacterial hydrolysis [47].

compound.teaching_note: Baicalin and baicalein interconvert in the body: the gut removes the glucuronide, the liver puts it back [47, 34].
gaps: Efficacy evidence not found for the isolated compound.
